why: Provenance and licence for the DEV SEED provider photos. Real Indian portraits, because the seeded directory is the only place anyone sees what this product looks like with people in it, and half the previous seed was not Indian at all (Amit, 2026-09-05, goal item 11).
scope: DEV SEED ONLY. These are stock photographs of real people used to populate a demo directory on a test project. They must never be shipped as production provider listings: the Pexels licence forbids implying that a person in a photo endorses a product, and a paid companionship listing is exactly that implication. A real provider uploads their own photo (useUploadAvatar). 2026-09-08: six ASTROLOGER portraits added (migration 085/087) on Amit's explicit instruction, after the constraint above was put to him twice. They are drawn from a different class of photograph than a keyword search returns first: POSED STUDIO PORTRAITS, not the candid street photography of rural elders that "indian senior man portrait" surfaces. That distinction is the mitigation and it is deliberate — a person who sat for a stock studio shoot expects commercial reuse, whereas a farmer photographed in a field did not, and attaching the second to a paid astrology listing with a manufactured 4.7 star rating is the case this paragraph was written about.

processing: Cropped to 3:4 from the top of the frame and resized to 900x1200. No other edit. 2026-09-08: the astrologer crops are FACE-CENTRED rather than cropped from the top — YuNet (opencv_zoo face_detection_yunet_2023mar) locates the face, and the 3:4 box is 4.6x the face height with the face 34% down. The card renders a 76dp CIRCLE with resizeMode cover, so only the middle ~75% of the frame survives; a top crop put one subject's face at 12% of the frame and she rendered as a distant figure. Reviewed as circles before upload, not as rectangles.
upload: The files sit next to this manifest so a fresh project can be seeded from a checkout. Push them with: supabase storage cp --linked --experimental seed/providers/<file> ss:///avatars/seed/<file>

casting: Every subject must read as an adult and no older than 35 — the seeded providers are 26 to 34, and a photo that reads a decade off its profile makes the directory look fake before anyone reads a word of it. `apparent_age` is the reviewer's honest read of the photograph, recorded so it can be compared to the profile instead of remembered. It is not a claim about the person.
naming: The filename carries the content hash because the bucket cannot replace an object at an existing key — `storage rm` deletes nothing and `cp` has no upsert — and public objects are served with max-age=3600, so overwriting would hand out the old face for an hour. A content-addressed name makes both problems unrepresentable: a new photo is a new URL, and the URL can be cached forever. A contract test checks each name against its own sha256.
